payload.summary: Two defects hit live on the 2026-08-23T15:37Z dev-team tick, SLS lane. (1) SLS claim PRIMARY re-validates no gate, so it auto-claimed a row outside its quarantine class. (2) The row-prose-ceiling guard then made the correct revert impossible - 2nd live instance of an already-designed defect.

defect_1.detail: PRIMARY selects rows purely on promoted_by == "dev-team (supervised-lane sweep)" and re-checks NONE of the gates the promote script applied. FIX-AUDITOR-NOTEBOOK-APPEND-GATE-BYPASSED-ALL-GREEN-WRITE was stamped 2026-08-08T04:51:52Z and has since sat in ready[] carrying plan_only=false. effective_plan_only is FALSE (verified: absent from backlog-detail.json AND from every archive shard, board field false), so the row is outside SLS's supervised-AND-plan_only class - yet PRIMARY claimed it 15 days later on the stamp alone.
defect_1.why_it_matters: main.md's own Lane x Gate matrix routes ready[] sup=T po=F to READY-XOR-SUP-OR-PLANONLY, i.e. PO's HUMAN-GATED manual-dispatch sweep, and states the rationale explicitly: auto-dispatching a supervised:true dev-role row would defeat the reason the flag exists. PRIMARY's stamp-only selector silently bypasses that human gate. A stamp is a historical fact; eligibility is a current one. Any row ever stamped by SLS is permanently auto-claimable regardless of how its flags change afterwards.
defect_1.sibling: Same selector, same root cause as the already-recorded null-dispatch_lane defect (PRIMARY reads $picked.dispatch_lane verbatim with no null-guard). That one is the LANE half; this is the GATE half. A single re-validation pass in PRIMARY closes both.
defect_1.suggested_fix: PRIMARY must re-apply the promote script's own gates (effective_supervised, effective_plan_only, NOT is_epic_wrapper, deps_satisfied, NOT detail-DEFERRED) against CURRENT state before claiming, and re-resolve dispatch_lane via resolved_dispatch_lane($detail_items). FALLBACK already does exactly this - PRIMARY is the odd one out.

defect_2.existing_design: scripts/architect-20260823-orch-prose-ceiling-row-handoff.jq, defect D3 (labelled NEW/UNREPORTED in that brief, dated today)
defect_2.detail: The correct remediation for the bad claim was a lane-move in_progress[] -> ready[]. It was HARD-REJECTED: the guard looks up the live baseline ONLY in the 3 guarded lanes (backlog/ready/review), so a row arriving from in_progress[] gets liveBytes=0 and a zero-content-change lane-move reads as pure net-new growth (live=0B, candidate=26552B, exit 1).
defect_2.significance: This is the SECOND live instance, after the UC-CCA-P3 in_progress->review case the brief itself cites. It confirms D3 is a live generator, not a one-off: ANY over-ceiling row in in_progress[]/qa[]/active_sprints[] is permanently unmovable, and the affected rows are precisely the biggest ones. It also blocks the documented remediation for defect 1 above, so the two compound.
defect_2.workaround_used_this_tick: Marked the row BLOCKED with a populated blocked_reason IN PLACE. wip_in_progress excludes BLOCKED, so the WIP slot is freed and all four pickers stay unblocked. This works only because the guard does not inspect in_progress[] at all - the same blind spot that caused the rejection. Explicitly a workaround, not a fix: the row is still in the wrong lane.
defect_2.note: The brief's own RETURN PATH says to ship its section 3 FIRST and ALONE as a read-only predicate change. This tick is live evidence for that sequencing.
